source_datasets.name: ZamStats 2022 CPH Series B Religion Descriptive Tables, table B.1: population (de facto) by religion affiliation and province

licence.name: ZamStats census report, open download; no explicit reuse licence stated

source_datasets.citation: Zambia Statistics Agency, 2022 Census of Population and Housing, Series B Religion Descriptive Tables, Table B.1.
source_datasets.redistribution_limits: The census PDF is not committed; the derived public product attributes ZamStats and links the source.
source_datasets.notes: Table B.1 gives the de facto population in ten religion groups for the ten provinces plus the Zambia row; parsed with pdftotext -layout. The printed column header lists the questionnaire code order, which is inconsistent with the census's own analytical figures; the adopted column assignment (African Traditional 30,502; Judaism 463; Other Religious Groups 9,238; Non-Religious 233,260 national) is the unique reading consistent with figures 3.13-3.16 of the 2022 National Analytical Report and with tables B.2/B.3. Every person is allocated to one of the ten groups, so no not-stated residual exists. District tables (B.4/B.5) publish only Christianity against a bundled remainder and cannot separate no religion.

source_datasets.citation: Central Statistical Office of Zambia, 2010 Census of Population and Housing, Provincial Analytical Reports (ten volumes), Figure 4.10.
source_datasets.redistribution_limits: The census PDFs are not committed; the derived public product attributes ZamStats and links the source.
source_datasets.notes: Each provincial report prints figure 4.10 with five percentage data labels (Protestant, Catholic, Muslim, Other, None; percent of the province's population, one decimal). Counts are not published at province level, so the 2010 wave ships percentages only. The reports were published after the 2011 provincial reform and tabulate the 2010 census on the current ten provinces, including Muchinga.

indicators.label: Census population denominator
indicators.description: 2022: de facto province total in table B.1. 2010: census population by province from the 2022 National Analytical Report comparison table (context for the percent-only wave).
indicators.method: 2022: table B.1 province total. 2010: section 2.3 comparison table of the 2022 National Analytical Report.
indicators.spatial_coverage: Zambia provinces (geoBoundaries ADM1) as re-tabulated on the post-2011 ten-province structure.
indicators.quality_notes: 2022 percentages use the table B.1 de facto province total as the denominator; every person is allocated to one of the ten religion groups, so there is no not-stated category to exclude. 2010 values are the percentages printed in each provincial analytical report's figure 4.10 (percent of the province's population, one decimal); counts are not published at province level for 2010.

indicators.label: Religious affiliation %
indicators.description: Share of persons declaring any named religion.
indicators.method: 2022: 100 * (sum of the nine named-religion groups) / province de facto total. 2010: Protestant + Catholic + Muslim + Other as printed in figure 4.10.
indicators.quality_notes: 2022 percentages use the table B.1 de facto province total as the denominator; every person is allocated to one of the ten religion groups, so there is no not-stated category to exclude. 2010 values are the percentages printed in each provincial analytical report's figure 4.10 (percent of the province's population, one decimal); counts are not published at province level for 2010.

indicators.label: No religion %
indicators.description: Share of persons reporting no religion.
indicators.method: 2022: 100 * Non-Religious / province de facto total (column assignment reconciled against the analytical-report figures). 2010: the None percentage as printed in figure 4.10.
indicators.quality_notes: 2022 percentages use the table B.1 de facto province total as the denominator; every person is allocated to one of the ten religion groups, so there is no not-stated category to exclude. 2010 values are the percentages printed in each provincial analytical report's figure 4.10 (percent of the province's population, one decimal); counts are not published at province level for 2010.
